description: The UI state matrix (plans/UK-02.md §4, plans/UK-02b.md): layer (c) of every UI kit, pinned once for every language. Component rows: drive the headless model of expect.component with input (a member input omits takes vocabulary.defaults) and compare state, the sorted copy keys and the sorted actions (absent means none). A state is a components.json state of the component, or hidden: the drop-in renders nothing and a styled part renders empty; hidden appears only on rows that turn a service off. copy lists the keys this input shows: a subset of the state's components.json list plus core.* keys the input selects (D7); vocabulary.unreached names the listed keys no row can show yet. actions are the controls the copy names (vocabulary.actionKeys) plus replace-in-browser. vocabulary.gaps declares the variants not pinned yet, each with the work package that appends its rows. mustNot marks a negative case (UI-KITS §4.1): the expectation holds and none of its states, copy or actions appear. Inline sign-in rows have a sheet twin with the same expectation (D4); each must component has a presentation-absent twin of its default row (D6). theme rows pin UI-KITS §1.2 and §3.4's resolution; i18n rows the catalog lookup (the locale's override, the locale's table, the English override, English; a locale with no pack is English, and a pending core pack is English core copy) and the ICU subset, where # is the integer in plain ASCII digits (expect is computed by the generator's own formatter). vocabulary.loadingDelay pins DL7's delayed response: a row whose input has elapsedMs below min expects its loading state with no copy; from max, the state's usual copy. cli is the terminal drop-in contract (plans/UK-51.md), one object rather than component rows: verbs (the end-user set a mount offers, the developer verbs it offers only by name, the aliases), mount and help (what registering into a host CLI mounts, refuses with polaris-verb-collision, skips, hides and lists), gate (every licenseStatus x tty x json x entitled: run, the inline flow, or a refusal that is a triangle with its fix and exits 4), outcomes (a kit verb in a vocabulary.cli.situations situation: its mark, exit, result fields, stdout and fix verbs), stdin (what activate with no key reads, per vocabulary.cli.stdinKinds), capabilities (environment x streams x flags) and exit (the exit table). vocabulary.cli holds the rules; mount, help, gate and capabilities are computed by the generator's references. Every runner runs every row of every family; a row a natural model fails goes back as a bug against the row or the model. Append-only within a uiMatrixVersion: a changed row, input member or rule bumps it.

actions.open-card: Start the sign-in on the hosted card in the browser (Continue in browser, Continue with email).
actions.open-browser: Open the sign-in already in flight in the browser again; never a second request (Open browser again, the code view's Open browser).
actions.replace-in-browser: Replace a device on the card, for a form set to `replace: browser`.
actions.open-manage-url: Open the refusal's `manageUrl` or the account's device page in the browser.
actions.start-sign-in: Start the kit's own sign-in, from a refusal that only a sign-in fixes (Sign in to that account).
actions.copy-link: Copy the sign-in link or the address to the clipboard.
actions.retry: Repeat the step that failed or lapsed (Try again, Reconnect, Sign in again, Get a new code).
actions.cancel: Leave the step or the flow (Cancel).
actions.unlock: Unlock the synced data: submit the recovery code, or open its screen (Unlock, Unlock sync).
actions.start-over: Open the confirmation that replaces the sync key (Start over).
actions.confirm-start-over: Replace the sync key after the warning that synced data will be lost (T22).
actions.accept-ring-change: Confirm the changed ring that was shown: hand `served` to `acceptRingChange`, never a fresh read.
actions.use-recovery-code: Open the recovery code screen from the ring confirmation.
actions.copy-code: Copy the recovery code to the clipboard.
actions.keep-local: Resolve a save conflict by keeping the copy on this device (Keep this device's version).
actions.keep-remote: Resolve a save conflict by keeping the other copy, or accepting its deletion (Keep the other version, Delete it here too).
actions.keep-both: Resolve a save conflict by keeping both: the other copy is saved under a new name (Keep both).
actions.choose-again: Return a failed save conflict to its choices; nothing is applied (Choose again).

inputs.integrator: The integrator's theme identity: {name?, shortName?, developer?, accent? (a colour or core), accentDark?, icon?: bool, deviceCodeUrl?, poweredBy?: line | badge}. Absent: none set.
inputs.presentation: Discovery's core.presentation through PresentationSource (HA-12): {name, developerName?, accent?, accentDark?, icon: bool}, icon meaning verified bytes arrived; null when discovery carries none.
inputs.bundle: The app bundle's identity: {slug, name?}. The kit's last identity source.
inputs.platform: {os, formFactor}: the device the kit runs on.
inputs.services: The enabled opt-in services (tools/services.json slugs), closed under `requires`. Absent: all on.
inputs.capabilities: What the build offers: {signIn, keyEntry, deviceCode, offlineActivation, trial, restore, purchase, enroll}; a member a row omits takes the default.
inputs.stage: The boot stage machine (stage-matrix.json): {stage, outcome, emit?}, emit one of its emit objects.
inputs.gate: The gate: {status?: licenseStatus, checking?: true (no status yet), cached?: true (a cached license is being re-checked), graceDaysLeft?, allowed?: {min?, max?} (the license's allowed versions)}.
inputs.pending: The action in flight, which drives the busy states.
inputs.loading: true while the component's data loads.
inputs.elapsedMs: Milliseconds since the request a loading state waits on started (DL7, vocabulary.loadingDelay). Below min the state shows nothing; from max its usual copy. Absent: the delay has passed.
inputs.keyField: The license key field: {text, submitted?}. A key is `pkey_<slug>_` and a 22-character secret.
inputs.activation: An activation result: {result: activationResult, code?, limit?, deviceCount?, manageUrl?}.
inputs.offline: Offline activation: {copied?, file?, submitted?, verified?} (the request code copied, a response loaded, submitted, its signature verified).
inputs.provider: The sign-in provider's name (Apple, Google, Steam), for the strings that name it: the link offer, the failed sign-in. Absent: Polaris Locker, the sign-in the generic row opens.
inputs.autoSignIn: Automatic sign-in's step in the sign-in form (needs signIn): {step: confirm | link-offer | link-done | link-conflict | nearby-prompt | nearby-wait | nearby-done | nearby-choose | nearby-none-found | nearby-denied | nearby-expired | nearby-not-nearby | nearby-failed | nearby-rate-limited | nearby-unavailable | nearby-cancelled | nearby-signed-out | device-limit, email?, kind? (the exchange that made the grant: apple | google | gamecenter | pgs; absent after a Polaris Locker sign-in), reach?: global | developer | unknown, manageUrl? (device-limit: where a device is replaced)}. No email: the provider shared none, and the confirm line follows `kind`. The provider is `provider`.
inputs.nearbyApproval: The approving device's side of nearby sign-in: {step: entry | ask | approved | not-nearby | mismatch | denied | expired | device-limit | choose | account-required | rate-limited | listening | stopped | failed, device?}. Absent: the account-menu entry. `listening` is the screen open with nothing asking yet; `stopped` the advert stopped after declined requests; `failed` a server or network failure.
inputs.linkPairing: Pairing with someone nearby: {step: open | code | confirm | linked | failed | unavailable, device?, code?, categories?, reason?: declined | timeout | full | closed}. `device` is the label the other device reported: nothing authenticates it, so the screen words it as reported and, without one, says the device gave no name. `code` is drawn as served and compared by both people. `categories` (ids, at most 8) are listed before the confirm button; none says nothing is shared yet. `unavailable`: links are off for the product (the typed connect_links_disabled). Absent: LinkPairing is hidden.
inputs.transferOffer: A contact's offer to send something (D-8, consent per transfer): {step: ask | receiving | done | failed, device?, name}. `device` is the contact's label and `name` what it offers, both text the other side chose. Absent: TransferOffer is hidden.
inputs.signIn: The sign-in session: {presentation, replace, channel, outcome?, browserOpened?, redeeming?, event?, issuedNow?, raced?, grantExpired?}. outcome is session.wait()'s; issuedNow is true when this sign-in added or issued the license.
inputs.deviceCode: The device-code poll: {phase, secondsLeft?}. Present exactly on rows with signIn.channel device-code; it alone selects SignInHandoff's state.
inputs.selected: The row the person picked in LicenseChoice (a licence id, keep or create). Absent: the view's preselected.
inputs.devices: The license's devices: [{name, platform, formFactor, lastSeenDays, current}].
inputs.browserMode: true when device management is in the browser only.
inputs.edit: An inline edit the person opened: {kind: rename | remove | value, device?}.
inputs.saved: true just after a save succeeded.
inputs.replacement: A Replace a device on the key path: {device, outcome: done | failed}.
inputs.update: The update decision and its download: {action: updateAction, outlet?: outletKind, reason?, version?, mandatory?, critical?, progress?: {phase, fraction?}}.
inputs.config: config.list rows: [{key, type, source, locked, org?, value?, min?, max?, advanced?}].
inputs.account: {signedIn, holder?: account}: holder is the account signed in on this device (S-19), or absent.
inputs.offers: {available, purchased?, url?}: url is the https page that sells the offer outside the app (a store page or the product's Polaris Locker page), from the integrator or the server; the hand-off shows only when the opener accepts it (DL14).
inputs.toast: {kind, closesIn?, left?}: the toast being shown. `left` (key-entries): the key entries the license has left.
inputs.error: {code}: a core.codes code the step failed with.
inputs.cloudSync: CloudSyncStatus's state: {state: synced | syncing | offline | conflict | error | locked | ring-changed | transferring | waiting | transfer-failed, signedIn?, canReview?, lastSynced?, transfer?: {size?, total?, fraction?}, reason?: network | battery | background}. `ring-changed` always offers Review: the kit owns the confirmation. `transferring` shows `transfer.size` of `transfer.total` (display-ready sizes) when both are given, and a bar that is determinate only with `transfer.fraction` (counted bytes, 0 to 1); `waiting` names its `reason` (default network); `transfer-failed` offers Try again. While a transfer is pending the status never says Synced, whatever `lastSynced` holds.
inputs.saveConflict: SaveConflict: {step: choose | keeping | kept | failed, local?: {when?}, remote?: {when?, device?} | null, bothAvailable?, keep?: local | remote | both, newer?: local | remote}. `remote: null` means the other copy was deleted: Keep the other becomes Delete it here too and Keep both is not offered. `bothAvailable` is true only with a free slot of the 16; absent or false draws Keep both disabled, with its reason. `keep` is the choice being applied (keeping), applied (kept) or that failed; kept needs it. `reopened`: true on choose when a choice met a newer copy and nothing was applied; one line says the other version changed again. `newer`: `local | remote`, the version the app knows was saved later (its own metadata, never the display strings). It tags that card and chooses nothing; it is ignored when the other copy was deleted. `when` and `device` are display-ready.
inputs.licenseHolder: Who holds the license a key just activated: {email?}. No email (or an empty one): floating, held by the key alone. An email: the license was sent to it and no account holds it yet (waiting); screens mask it. `addIn: portal` (UK-43.2): the kit has no in-app channel for Add your name and email, so the Add control of ActivateDone, SignIn `key-done` and AccountAndLicense's floating row says Add it in Polaris Locker (an external link) and opens the manage URL; absent or `app`: the in-app form. Absent: the holder is not known and AccountAndLicense draws what it drew before.
inputs.activateDone: The Done step after a key activates: {tier?, term?, deviceKind?, position?, limit?}, the strings and numbers the license line shows. Absent: ActivateDone is hidden. The state is `waiting` with a `licenseHolder` email and Identity on, else `ready`; the reasons follow the services (Cloud Sync only with sync, Get your license back and Move it with Identity, else the portal line).
inputs.addToAccount: Add your name and email: {step: form | invalid | busy | added | owned | email-bound | other-account | failed, field?: name | email | both, deviceKind?, typedEmail?, signedEmail?, fromSettings?}. `invalid` names the field to fix (absent: both). owned: someone attached the license meanwhile; email-bound: the license was sent to another email (with `licenseHolder`); other-account: a different account signed in than the email typed (`typedEmail` and `signedEmail`, both masked); `fromSettings` closes `added` with Done; failed: sign-in or attach did not finish. `added` names Cloud Sync only with sync on. Absent: AddToAccount is hidden.
inputs.unlockSync: UnlockSync's step: {step: code | invalid | working | failed | start-over-failed | no-code | start-over, nearby?}. `no-code`: the account has no recovery code, so only Start over helps. `nearby` says the host could unlock from a nearby device; v0.10.0 never offers it (NearbyApproval does not ship).
inputs.recoveryCode: RecoveryCode: {saved?}. The code itself is never an input of the view: the kit draws it from the host, once, and keeps nothing.
inputs.ringChange: RingChange: {by?, served?: {ringId, epoch, rootKid}, failed?}. `failed`: accepting the ring did not open a root; the screen says so and Accept stays available. `by` is the name of the device that wrapped (`changed.by`); `served` is the ring the person was shown (`changed.served`), the one value `acceptRingChange` takes. No `served`: nothing to accept, only the recovery code.

precedence.LicenseChoice: loading, grant-expired, raced, replace-open (open-replace with replace inline), none-keys or none-no-keys (state none), new (state autoIssue), create (create selected), all-full (no free row), keep, current, mixed (account and seat licences together), one, many.
precedence.SignIn: error, auto (autoSignIn), expired, done (signedIn), key-refused or key (have-key while choosing; the key-entry limit and an owned license are key-refused), replace (open-replace with replace inline), choose, finishing (redeeming, or device-code ok), code (device code, or use-code), handoff (pending), methods.
precedence.Settings: loading, error, saving (pending save or saved), dirty, locked (a locked row), list.
precedence.Devices: loading, error, browser-mode, renaming or confirming (edit), empty, list.
precedence.ActivateDone: hidden (License off), waiting (a licenseHolder email, Identity on), ready (the reasons follow the services).
precedence.AddToAccount: hidden (Identity off), then the step: form, invalid, busy, added, owned, email-bound, other-account, failed.
precedence.SignIn (holders): `signIn.step` key-done (the ActivateDone body), attach (AddToAccount's, at its `addToAccount.step`) or added wins over every step except error and an automatic sign-in step.
precedence.AccountAndLicense (holders): key-only with a `licenseHolder` that has no email (floating) draws Not in an account and Add your name and email instead of the key-only line; Identity off keeps it, Add opening the portal.
precedence.LinkPairing: hidden (Connect off or no linkPairing), then the step: open, code (a device reached the code), confirm, linked, failed (its reason picks the line), unavailable.
precedence.TransferOffer: hidden (Connect off or no transferOffer), then the step: ask, receiving, done, failed.
precedence.Paywall: loading, purchasing (pending purchase), restore (pending restore), purchased, not-available, offers.

mustNot.PolarisKeyGate: flash activation during a cached-session check
mustNot.Boot: animate invented progress, or trap metered consent off-screen
mustNot.SignIn: restart the flow or erase account context on a step change
mustNot.SignInHandoff: use the public user code as the polling handle
mustNot.NearbyApproval: approve on any code but the one the other device shows
mustNot.Activate: require an account for a floating key
mustNot.OfflineActivation: treat a loaded file as a verified activation
mustNot.DeviceLimit: delete local files when access is removed
mustNot.LicenseChoice: blur keep, create and add-to-account into one outcome
mustNot.Devices: say "This device" when the runtime does not know it
mustNot.UpdatePrompt: offer a restart the browser cannot perform on a desktop product
mustNot.UpdateProgress: say installed when only the download verified
mustNot.StatusScreen: collapse the five refusals into one error
mustNot.Settings: expose hidden values through a theme
mustNot.EntitlementGate: treat a style override as authorization
mustNot.Toast: be the only record of an error

SignIn.code.signin.code.resend: The card's email-code step (SIGN-IN.md §3.4, §4.16). Credentials are entered only on the card (S-16 D17); the kit form's `code` step is the device-code view, which SignInHandoff draws.

SignInHandoff.waiting.signin.handoff.check: The device-code match line. Device-code `waiting` selects `code` (plans/UK-02b.md §4.5), whose list lacks it; components.json is reconciled by the next catalog package.

sections.verbs: Verb ids are a verb's words joined with a space. endUser is the default mount; developer verbs mount only when options.verbs names them; aliases maps another name to a one-word verb.
sections.mount: Register the kit's verbs into a host CLI whose own top-level commands are input.host, with input.options. mounted: the commands the host gains, as typed (namespace first). error: the registration error (nothing is mounted): every host command equal to a namespace, a verb's first word or an alias, and the two options that resolve it. skipped: the verbs onCollision skip dropped; the kit warns once, naming them. hidden: the options help hides once config is given. The host's own commands are never renamed, removed or re-described.
sections.help: The root help page's sections in order: the host's, under its headings, then one section whose heading is the kit copy key `copy` with what the mount added at the top level (a namespace is one entry). commands is each section's set; within a section the kit keeps its order.
sections.gate: requireLicense(handler, {entitlement?}) before the host's command input.command. run: the action runs and exits as it does. flow: the kit's activate or sign-in flow runs inline, then the action. refuse: mark, the title (copy; {command} is input.command; no message line, because the fix follows), then link (portal: the product page, from the kit's portal URL; contact: `status.contact` with the developer's name, where the kit resolves no product page, WIRE-CONTRACT-V4 section 5.7: input.portal is false) and the fix verbs as command rows, written once to stream (stderr: no escape off a terminal), the exit; fix is the verbs filtered by input.mounted (absent: the end-user set), and a link stands in when none is left. fail: input.check (the check throws, or answers a status that is not a licenseStatus) draws a cross with copy (title and message), no fix row, exit 4. With --json stdout carries only `result`, the envelope's result line (CLI_JSON_VERSION 1).
sections.outcomes: Drive the kit's verb in input.situation (situations) on a Unicode terminal (json false) or with --json, and compare: exit; mark, the outcome's step mark (that symbol is drawn and the other of fail and warn is not); error and code, the result's fields (null: no error); stdout (empty: nothing on stdout; screen: the flow is drawn on stdout; result: only JSON lines, the last the result); fix, the verb ids of the command rows drawn, as a set; link, the row drawn where no fix verb is (portal: the product page link; contact: `status.contact` with the developer's name, where the kit resolves no product page, WIRE-CONTRACT-V4 section 5.7 - a situation whose name ends -no-page sets up a client whose discovery says the portal is off; an `activate` row of that kind and no link draws neither the link nor a contact row, its success stands alone).
sections.stdin: activate with no key, stdin of kind input.stdin (stdinKinds) given input.lines, each followed by a newline (null: nothing is written and the writer stays open). read: prompt (the masked entry), key (the first non-empty line, here the fixture key, without waiting for the writer to close) or none (the copy key, the exit, the error, and with withinMs the run ends, process and all, within that many milliseconds). The none screen is drawn on stdout, like every kit verb's screen (outcomes stdout: screen); stderr is the gate's, because a gated host command's stdout is the host's.
sections.capabilities: detectTerminal over input.env, the streams (tty or pipe) and the flags (color false is --no-color), to colour, unicode, interactive, animate and links.
sections.exit: The exit codes every terminal kit uses.

marks.fail: A cross: a failure, with what happened.
marks.warn: A triangle: a refusal the person can resolve, with its fix (DL6).

errors.license_required: A refused gate: the license is not usable, or the version is outside its allowed range.
errors.not_entitled: A refused gate: the license does not include the channel, or the entitlement the gate asks for.

situations.status-revoked: `status` on a device signed in to an account, whose license the server revoked.
situations.status-version-too-old: `status`: this version is below the license's allowed range.
situations.status-version-too-new: `status`: this version is above the license's allowed range.
situations.status-channel-not-entitled: `status`: the license does not include this build's channel.
situations.status-version-too-new-no-page: `status`: this version is above the license's allowed range, and the product's discovery says its portal is off (`core.portal` is `{enabled:false}`).
situations.status-channel-not-entitled-no-page: `status`: the license does not include this build's channel, and the product's discovery says its portal is off (`core.portal` is `{enabled:false}`).
situations.activate-floating: `activate`, a well-formed key on a piped stdin, the license is held by the key alone (no account on this device, no address on the license) and Identity is on: after the success, the recommendation title and the product page link (never `#key=`).
situations.activate-floating-no-page: `activate`, as `activate-floating`, and the product's discovery says its portal is off (`core.portal` is `{enabled:false}`): the success alone, no recommendation line.
situations.activate-waiting: `activate`, as `activate-floating`, but the license was sent to an address and no account holds it: the masked address and the `login` command row.
situations.activate-identity-off: `activate`, as `activate-floating`, with Identity off for the product: the portal reason and the product page link.
situations.status-floating: `status` on a license held by the key alone (no account on this device, no address on the license): the license row says it is not in an account, and the product page link follows.
situations.network: `devices list`: the request fails with the registry code `network`.
situations.key-refused: `activate`, a well-formed key on a piped stdin: the server answers 401 `unauthorized`.
situations.device-limit: `activate`, a well-formed key on a piped stdin: the server answers `device_limit` with a `manageUrl`; no key reader, so the flow ends.
situations.secret-hidden: `secret api_key` for a secret that is set, without `--reveal`.
situations.interrupt: `activate` on an interactive terminal with no key: Ctrl-C at the key prompt.
situations.sign-in-cancelled: `login` on an interactive terminal: Esc while it waits for the browser.
situations.sign-in-denied: `login`: the device-code poll answers `error` with `reason: access_denied`.
situations.sign-in-failed: `login`: the device-code poll answers a bare `error` (no `reason`).
situations.sign-in-nearby: `login` on an interactive terminal, nearby on: an approver answers within 2 s, the code is shown and the person taps it on the other device. With `--json` nearby never starts (no browse, no LAN request): the device-code flow runs and signs in.
situations.sign-in-nearby-handoff: `login` on an interactive terminal, nearby on: no approver answers within 2 s, so nearby is cancelled and the regular sign-in runs and signs in.
situations.approve-approved: `devices approve` on an interactive terminal, signed in: a device nearby asks, the person taps the code it shows (one of three) and the device is signed in.
situations.approve-mismatch: `devices approve`: the person taps a code the other device does not show; the request is denied.
situations.approve-denied: `devices approve`: the person chooses Deny; the request is denied.
situations.approve-not-nearby: `devices approve`: the Worker answers that the device that asked is not on this network (`not_nearby`).
situations.approve-unsupported: `devices approve` on a runtime that cannot take part in the nearby handshake (CC-15 answers `nearby-unsupported`).
situations.approve-account-required: `devices approve` on a device that is signed out: there is no account to approve for.
situations.approve-json: `devices approve --json`: both sides need a person, so the run is refused before anything starts.

stdinKinds.tty: A terminal, on an interactive run.
stdinKinds.tty-noninteractive: A terminal, on a run that cannot prompt (`CI` is truthy).
stdinKinds.socket: A socket: what a Node parent's pipe is (`spawn`, `execSync({ input })`, execa).
stdinKinds.char-device: A character device such as /dev/null: never read.

holdersFlow.description: AddToAccountModel's flow (UK-43.2), mirrored from ui-core's test/addToAccountModel.test.ts: a scripted driver answers (waits, complete, preview, attach), the actions are pressed in order, and the model's step after each, the driver's calls and hints, and the final view's state are pinned. Typed values are fields.name and fields.email (default Ada Lovelace, ada@example.com); they never appear in a view's input. calls: signIn (the start), complete:<grant>:keep, preview (attach with confirm false), attach (confirm true, no address), cancel (the sign-in is let go). A driver call past its script answers ok (preview, attach) or cancelled (waits). maskEmail pins the masking every screen uses: the first character, three dots, the domain; an address it cannot mask is the empty string.
